name: multi-user-synthetic
description: Multi-user linear bandit: 5 instances of 100 users in 5 clusters, 500 actions in R^10, 20 random actions offered per step (as in CLUB and SCLUB), 2 runs each. LinUCB shared, per user, and per user with k-means clusters (5 clusters), against CLUB and SCLUB. Theoretical defaults.

policies.label: LinUCB
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: LinUCB_IND
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: LinUCB_IND_KMeans
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: CLUB
notes: alpha=1.0 (exploration weight, tuned on the data in the paper)
lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)
cluster_alpha=2.0 (tuned on the data in the paper)

policies.label: SCLUB
notes: cluster_alpha: 4 R sqrt(d / lambda_x), lambda_x from the actions offered
lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: Values of the papers: LinUCB alpha=1, LinUCB_IND alpha=1, LinUCB_IND_KMeans alpha=1, SCLUB alpha=1. They give the theoretical confidence bounds: safe in theory, but they often explore too much in practice. To fit them to this problem, run a grid search (param_grid=True, or "param_grid": true in a config file) or set them, e.g. LinUCB(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: k-means users (heuristic)
notices.text: LinUCB_IND_KMeans keeps one model per user and pulls its estimate towards the centroid of its cluster, with weight n_u / (n_u + cluster size). The clusters come from a k-means on the user estimates (n_user_clusters clusters, recomputed every user_recluster_freq steps). This shares what similar users learned, without a regret guarantee.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: Pseudo-regret (track "pseudo_regret"); action of every step (track "actions"); peak memory (measure_memory=True). The dashboard and the figures cannot show what is not stored; the brackets say how to store it (in a config file: "track": [...] or "measure_memory": true in "experiment").

notices.title: One point every 50 steps
notices.text: Curves keep one point every 50 steps and the last step (log_interval=50). The values at these points are exact. Between two points, the charts draw a straight line: there the curve is interpolated, not measured. log_interval=1 keeps every step (larger files).

notices.title: Parallel runs
notices.text: With n_jobs=4, each process uses one BLAS thread: compare CPU times only between runs with the same n_jobs.
